commit e25152741388506884dfebbc4a353d97f45fbaa4
Author:     Suin Park <bamtolsuin@pusan.ac.kr>
AuthorDate: Tue Nov 3 16:00:43 2026 +0900
Commit:     Suin Park <bamtolsuin@pusan.ac.kr>
CommitDate: Tue Nov 3 16:00:43 2026 +0900

    feat(doppler): exact Maxwell average for Doppler-on Lambda and Rydberg
    
    User decision (consolidation item 4c): drop the 2 m/s, 4 sigma velocity grid
    for the exact Maxwell average.
    
    AffineScan.maxwell_mean takes the Gaussian mean of the pole form in closed
    form with sigma = k sqrt(k_B T/m): no grid, no truncation. It matches fine
    trapezoid grids to <=2e-12 (Lambda), 5.7e-11 (Rydberg EIT) and 2.3e-9 (Rydberg
    AT electrometry) at the 4b cost (13 ms Lambda, 19 ms Rydberg). Rows that miss
    the pole guard, or the whole scan on LinAlgError, are summed on a grid whose
    step resolves the rows' narrowest pole: doppler.maxwell_strip_grid, step
    2 pi strip / (k ln(1/error)), error 1e-8, +-6 sigma. magneto's fallback grid
    now comes from the same function, bit-identical.
    
    The superheterodyne finite-IF phasor is a product of complex (L - i omega_IF)
    resolvents with no closed form, so it stays a class sum, now on the pole-derived
    grid (AffineScan.quadrature_classes, solved in chunks of 16384 classes). It is
    within 6.1e-7 of a finer grid (error 1e-11, 8 sigma) at every slider end; a
    readout takes about 0.2 s and the cell-heating sweep's first run 2.3 s (0.39 s
    before).
    
    Correction to the 57bf5a2 checklist notes: the difference from the old grid is
    not the 4 sigma truncation. Widening to 8 sigma leaves it; the 2 m/s step makes
    it (k * 2 m/s = 2.56 MHz against the 2.87 MHz natural HWHM), and 1 m/s takes
    Lambda to 1e-6. The same step had the finite-IF phasor 58 % off.
    
    Value changes against 57bf5a2, Doppler on only:
    - Lambda: chi_bar up to ~0.15 %; displayed readouts at the regime defaults are
      unchanged at display precision.
    - Rydberg EIT: linewidth 2.92 -> 2.89 MHz, IF optimum -1.87 -> -1.33 MHz.
    - Rydberg AT electrometry: total sensitivity 1007.28 -> 1557.57 nV/cm/rtHz,
      RF AT splitting 2.39 -> 2.05 MHz, AT field estimate 99.44 -> 85.565 mV/m RMS,
      superheterodyne optimum -2.16 -> -2.28 MHz, response phase +3.8 -> +2.8 deg.
    - Cell heating: sensitivities rise about 54 % (55 C: 38.80 -> 59.44
      nV/cm/rtHz) and 55 C stays best; Fig. 2(b) moves up to 7.5 % in amplitude and
      2 % in width.
    This supersedes 57bf5a2's "1007.28 stands". cache_version becomes
    physical-units-v5-exact-maxwell and rydberg-eit-v7-exact-maxwell, which also
    covers 4b's value change. The stored analysis/rydberg_cell_heating results are
    Doppler off and do not move.
    
    Doppler off is bit-identical: 134612 displayed and extra-view paths, and the
    raw snapshots with and without Numba. Every recompute knob at both slider ends
    and every choice of Lambda EIT/AT/CPT and Rydberg EIT/AT electrometry, Doppler
    on: 132 calls, 92532 rows, no fallback row, worst row 6.2e-8 against a
    resolving grid. test_absorption's angle test had its independent reference
    pinned to the 2 m/s grid; it now uses 0.5 m/s and 8 sigma at the same 1e-10.
    docs/checklist.json records the decision and the validation on both pole items.
